axes.model_access: Digital-human video generation line: an official persona library + personal/enterprise custom digital humans (consented cloning) + a dubbing line (as seen in site navigation); the underlying models — no official statement verified item by item.
axes.runtime: Web (synthesia.io) + API (enterprise-facing, seen on the official site); generation on the vendor's cloud.
axes.local_files: Works stored account-side in the cloud (the enterprise surface has workspaces); downloads go local. No officially stated local data surface.
axes.background: Generation is instant/queued (varies by tier, not verified item by item); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified).
axes.tools: **Enterprise training video is the flagship scenario** (official narrative: L&D/compliance training/localization); a PPT/document-to-video line (seen on the official site), multilingual dubbing + lip-sync, SCORM and other enterprise-learning ecosystem integrations (seen on the official site).
axes.context: Organized via team workspaces (enterprise collaboration is one of the product's main axes); cross-session memory — no official statement verified.
axes.permissions: Subscription + enterprise system (D9: prices not collected); consent verification for custom digital humans is the key compliance surface (official consent narrative, details not verified line by line); free-tier feature and export limits follow the terms (not verified line by line).
axes.fit: Fits: enterprise L&D/compliance training videos, multilingual localization at scale, standardized talking-head video without on-camera talent. Does not fit: creative narrative, social entertainment, heavy personal free use (a subscription-first product posture).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **PPT-to-video conversion quality** (layout fidelity)
- **Actual compatibility of SCORM export with mainstream LMSs**
- **Consent verification and delivery cycle for custom digital humans**
unknowns:
- The underlying generation model (no official statement verified)
- The concrete limits of the free tier (not verified line by line)
- The training-use switch (not verified line by line)
- A compliant entry for mainland enterprise customers (unverified)
related: The two enterprise digital-human heavyweights: HeyGen is more flexible on cloning/translation, Synthesia's training ecosystem runs deeper.
Both digital-human talking heads: D-ID is light photo-driven, Synthesia's enterprise workspace is heavier.
Dubbing upstream/downstream: the talking track of digital-human video is often supplied by ElevenLabs-style TTS; Synthesia's built-in dubbing line is another path.
sources: Synthesia · official site (product and capability narrative)
